Row.Text: Has 2 slots Great Works of Music. Provides a free Cathedral in the city. Gives 1 free Great Person.
To maximize your bonus, make sure to have to have 2 Great Works Of Music from the same era and from your civilization.
[NEWLINE]"Every great architect is - necessarily - a great poet. He must be a great original interpreter of his time, his day, his age."[NEWLINE] - Frank Lloyd Wright[NEWLINE]

Montreal's Notre-Dame Basilica is one of the crown jewels in Quebec's rich religious heritage. Dedicated to Our Lady the Blessed Virgin – “Notre Dame” – the small original chapel was operated at first by the Jesuits. Then came the Sulpician Fathers, who in 1657 undertook construction of a larger church. The Sulpician François Dollier de Casson was its architect, and the present-day Notre-Dame Street served as the original site. Its construction, in Baroque style was completed between 1672 and 1683. [NEWLINE] By 1800, Dollier’s church had become too small, and the Fabrique decided to build the church we know today. To design the new church, the building council engaged the services of the New York architect James O’Donnell – himself an Irish Protestant by origin. O’Donnell and the Fabrique opted for the Gothic Revival style then in vogue in England and the United States. The main construction work took place between 1824 and 1829.
